text:
The aircraft maintenance scheduling problem
Multiple aircraft go through routine checks concurrentlyConcurrent maintenance creates dips in fleet availability. Staggered checks must preserve start windows and maintenance rules.Finite resources such as dock space, mechanics, and components.First: maximise worst-day availability.Then: reduce standard deviation.

text:
PRIORITY BASED SELECTION WITH VARIABLE NEIGHBOURHOOD SEARCH
Priority selection searches the worst availability regions first
Rank events by the worst availability during their interval.Search the worst priority level first, expand only if needed.Move one check, then rebuild later events using A/B/C/D rules.Update incrementally and score once.Deterministic, rule-compliant, and substantially faster.Measured result: min 15→18, std 1.96→1.44.

text:
MILESTONE 4 · HOW PRIORITY LEVELS WORK
Each event gets one priority: the worst day it covers
From the heavy starting schedule: global min availability = 15, 278 events, 24 aircraft
1. Score every event
Look at fleet availability on every day that event is in the hangar.Priority = the minimum of those days.Example: event days with availability: [18, 18, 16, 15, etc.] → priority 15.
2. Split into exclusive buckets
Level 15 → 20 events (touch a day-15 dip).Level 16 → 10 events Level 17 → 9 eventsLevel 21 → 68 events
3. Search worst first
Try only level-15 events × shifts (e.g. 20 × 2 = 40).If any move improves the score, stop and pick the best.Only then expand to 16, 17… if level 15 finds nothing.

text:
SIMULATED ANNEALING
What simulated annealing is 
1 · Search
Same priority-based selection neighbour search algorithm
2 · Accept
Better moves are always kept. Worse moves can still be kept early on, by chance.
3 · Cool down
Over time we accept fewer worse moves, so the search settles on a strong plan.
Why it helps
Think of the search like walking over hills. Today’s method only walks uphill. That is fast and safe, but you can get stuck on a steep part of the hill when a better peak is nearby.Simulated annealing sometimes takes a downhill step early, so you can leave a trap and reach a better overall schedule. As the search “cools,” those downhill steps become rare, and we settle on the best plan we found.

text:
LIMITS AND NEXT STEPS
The original worst-day target is already optimal
Original forecast
Six D checks must overlap in a fixed interval.With 24 aircraft, worst-day availability cannot exceed 18.The measured result reaches this bound.
Stagger datasets
The upper bound is 21 on each stagger dataset.Measured results reach 19 and 20.Those remaining gaps are unresolved.
Evidence boundary
Smoothness is locally optimal only. These are synthetic, maintenance-only benchmarks. A new fleet, regenerated check list, or changed rules needs a fresh study.
